Diagnosis: set_key (main.py:184-185) writes single-quoted values escaping only `'` → `\'`, but never escapes backslashes. The parser (parser.py:25,32,132) decodes `\\` and `\'` in single-quoted values via `decode_escapes`. So a literal `\` written raw is consumed as an escape: `a\b` → `ab`, `\\` → `\`, and a trailing `\` before the closing quote breaks parsing. Hence no round-trip.

Change plan: In set_key, when quoting, escape backslashes first, then apostrophes: `value_to_set.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")`. This matches the parser's `_single_quote_escapes` (`\\`, `\'`) and README lines 179. Leave `never` mode and export prefix untouched. No parser changes needed.
